sermons.title: Borrowed or Owned: What Do You Actually Believe About Sunday?
sermons.speaker: Trent Cornwell
sermons.notesHtml:
Introduction

At Crown College, someone told me it was okay to borrow someone else's conviction until you had your own.

I had borrowed mine. From my mom. Single mom. She worked hard and carried a lot. But Sunday was different. Sunday was set apart. There was a gravitational pull around that day I could not shake. Not messing with Sunday was somehow foundational to who I was. I didn't have the theology. I just had her.

A borrowed conviction will hold you for a while. Eventually life gets hard enough that you need something you actually own.

Today I'm not asking you to adopt my view of Sunday. I'm asking you to walk through the whole Bible on this question and come out the other side with something that belongs to you.

The Framework

  • The Passover was fulfilled for us — in Christ
  • The Law was fulfilled for us — in Christ
  • The Sabbath was fulfilled for us — in Christ

Two Extremes Nobody Here Actually Lives:

  1. Extreme 1 — Legalistic Sabbatarianism: Saturday kept under full Mosaic and rabbinic regulation. Five examples still practiced: no light switches, no carrying outside an eruv, no tearing paper, no cooking, no driving or machinery.
  2. Extreme 2 — Rest doesn't matter: Seven-day work weeks, no Lord's Day priority, no rhythm of rest. Physically: fatigue, burnout, breakdown. Spiritually: no time for God or family — leads to drift.

Most of us live between these. Not legalists. Not dismissers. Just people who inherited a Sunday habit and never examined it.

The Sabbath Was Always About More Than a Day

Two Hebrew Words:

SHABBAT — To stop working. Like clocking out at the end of a shift. NUAKH — To dwell. To settle. Like arriving at your grandmother's house for the holidays, putting your bag down, and exhaling. Rest as presence, not just cessation.

God didn't just stop working on Day Seven. He moved in with His people. The garden was the first dwelling place — rest as relationship.

Genesis 2:2–3 “2 And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. 3 And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.”

Two things to observe:

  1. Completion, not exhaustion — satisfaction in finished work
  2. Pre-Mosaic — before any law was given, before Moses, Israel, or Sinai Pattern, not command — a rhythm wired into creation itself

The Sabbath was never really about a day. It was always about a relationship.

Israel Got the Picture, But Missed the Point

The Manna Test — First Commanded Sabbath, Before Sinai:

Exodus 16:28–29 “28 And the LORD said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? 29 See, for that the LORD hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”

A covenant test for Israel specifically — not a universal creation command applied to all peoples.

Codified at Sinai:

Exodus 20:8–10 “8 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. 9 Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: 10 But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:”

Exodus 31:16–17 “16 Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. 17 It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.”

Key observations:

  1. Specific audience: Israel. Not the nations. Not the Church.
  2. Covenant sign — marking a specific people in a specific covenant
  3. Death penalty for violation — Exodus 31:14; Numbers 15:32-36 — civil/national law for a theocracy

The Second Grounding:

Deuteronomy 5:15 “15 And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.”

  1. Exodus 20 grounds the Sabbath in creation.
  2. Deuteronomy 5 grounds it in the Exodus from Egypt. That national/redemptive grounding makes no sense applied to Gentile believers.

Sabbath Year and Jubilee:

Leviticus 25:1–4 “1 And the LORD spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying, 2 Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the LORD. 3 Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; 4 But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.”

  1. Every seventh year: the land rested.
  2. Every 50th year (Jubilee): debts cancelled, property restored, slaves freed.

Civil/theocratic law for a land-owning nation under direct divine governance. Not transferable to the Church.

The Problem — The Picture Became the Prison:

By the time Jesus arrives, the Pharisees had buried the Sabbath under 613 regulations. The rest God intended had become an exhausting legal performance.

Matthew 11:28-29

Matthew places this BEFORE the Sabbath controversies in chapter 12. Jesus is not rescheduling the Sabbath — He is announcing He has become what it always pointed to.

Israel had the picture for 1,500 years. Then the reality showed up and said "Come to me."

Historical Books: The Ignored Sabbath

Nehemiah 13:18 “18 Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.”

Notice what Sabbath-breaking looked like:

  • Working in the fields
  • Hauling goods
  • Operating businesses
  • Buying and selling
  • Conducting normal commerce

Nehemiah's concern is not that they failed to attend worship services. His concern is that they ignored the covenant sign God had given Israel and treated the Sabbath like any other day.

Prophets: The Kingdom Sabbath

In the prophets we see it was ignored and also we see propphecy of it continuing during the millennial reign.

The Sabbath is not abolished in Colossians 2. It is fulfilled for this age. The prophets tell us it will be restored in the Kingdom under Christ's direct reign.

Isaiah 66:23 “23 And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD.”

Ezekiel 46:1 “1 Thus saith the Lord GOD; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened.”

The Church doesn't observe the Mosaic Sabbath because we are in a different period of God's redemptive plan — not because God forgot it. He never drops this thread.

The Sabbath Across Scripture — Five Periods:

  1. CREATION: Pattern established. Six and one. Work and rest.
  2. MOSAIC / ISRAEL: Formalised as covenant sign. Shadow pointing forward.
  3. CHURCH AGE — NOW: Fulfilled in Christ. Lord's Day. Liberty, not law.
  4. MILLENNIUM — FUTURE: Renewed under Christ's direct reign. All nations worship.
  5. NEW CREATION: Eternal Sabbath. God dwelling with His people. Revelation 21:3 “3 And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.”

The Sabbath runs from Genesis 2 all the way to the New Creation. God never drops this thread.

What Jesus Did to the Sabbath

1. Jesus Is Lord of the Sabbath:

Mark 2:27–28 “27 And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: 28 Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.”

  • Not correcting a technicality.
  • Asserting ownership over the whole institution.
  • If He is Lord over the Sabbath, He determines its meaning and its fulfillment.

Matthew 12:6 “6 But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.”

  • Greater than the temple = greater than everything the temple and its calendar pointed to.

2. The Finished Work:

Hebrews 10:1, Hebrews 10:9–10 “9 Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. 10 By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

Hebrews 4:9–10 “9 There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. 10 For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.”

  • The word in Hebrews 4:9 is sabbatismos — the only NT occurrence.
  • Sabbath-rest. Not a day on a calendar. A person. Entering His rest means ceasing from self-justification, striving, earning what Christ freely gives.

Which Day?

Sabbatarian Case — held by sincere Christians:

  • Fourth Commandment is in the Decalogue — moral law does not pass away Sabbath predates Sinai (Genesis 2) — not merely national/civil law
  • Matthew 5:17 — "I came not to destroy, but to fulfil" — they read this as uphold, not complete No explicit NT command changing the day from Saturday to Sunday
  • This view has been held by sincere, faithful Christians. We engage it respectfully.

Lord's Day Case — Three Anchor Texts:

1. Replace the shadow with the Person

Colossians 2:16–17 “16 Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: 17 Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

Paul calls the Sabbath days themselves a shadow — not the way you keep them. The substance is Christ. When you have the reality, the picture no longer binds.

2. Day-observance matter of liberty

Romans 14:5 “5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.”

Day-observance placed in the category of conscience and liberty. You cannot do that with "do not murder." That single placement is decisive.

3. Non binding law

Galatians 4:9–10 “9 But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? 10 Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.”

Paul's alarm is stunning. It only makes sense if the Mosaic calendar has passed as binding law for the Church.

The Resurrection Sunday

John 20:19 “19 Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.”

Think about John 20:19. The disciples are behind locked doors. Terrified.

  • The Sabbath has come and gone. Saturday ended with a sealed tomb and a scattered church.
  • Then — on the first day of the week — Jesus walks through the wall.
  • He chose that moment. He chose that day. The first Christian Sunday gathering was not planned by the apostles. It was called by the risen Christ Himself. John 20:26 “26 And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.”
  • He did it again the following Sunday with Thomas present.

The Sabbath rest was finished at the cross. The celebration of that rest began on Easter Sunday morning — and it has not stopped since.

The SDA Position — A Different Category:

A Christian who worships on Saturday out of personal conviction is your brother or sister. Romans 14 covers that. We differ, but the gospel we share is not undone by that difference.

The SDA system is a different matter — it has made Sabbath-keeping salvation-relevant:

Saturday Sabbath is a test of end-times loyalty — linked to the "mark of the beast" Investigative Judgment (1844) reviews believers' lives for worthiness — undermining the finished work of Christ Ellen White's writings carry quasi-authoritative status alongside Scripture

When the Sabbath is tied to salvation, it is no longer a liberty issue. It has become a gospel issue.

A believer with a Sabbatarian conviction is a brother. A system that makes Sabbath-keeping a test of salvation is a doctrinal error touching the gospel.

We didn't abolish the Sabbath. We fulfilled it — in Christ. And Christ is better than the shadow.

Therefore: Why We Gather on Sunday

The New Testament Pattern:

Acts 20:7 “7 And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.”

1 Corinthians 16:2 “2 Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.”

Revelation 1:10 “10 I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,”

What we lose is the legal obligation to observe Saturday with Mosaic regulations. What we gain is freedom to gather on the Lord's Day in resurrection joy — not from compulsion, but from love.

Early Church Confirmation:

  • Justin Martyr (c. AD 155): Christians gathered on Sunday because it is the day Jesus Christ rose from the dead.
  • Ignatius of Antioch (c. AD 110): Christians "no longer observe the Sabbath, but live according to the Lord's Day, on which our life has sprung up through Him."
  • Within one generation of the apostles. Apostolic pattern from the beginning — not a medieval Catholic invention.

A Pastoral Word:

I want to be honest about something I wrestle with as your pastor.

I want you to hold the Lord's Day in high esteem. I want Sunday to mean something to your family — a genuine weekly declaration that you belong to a risen Saviour.

But here is my tension: I can't bind your conscience where the New Testament gives you liberty. Romans 14 says the strong believer does not despise the one who esteems every day alike. I can't preach law where God has preached grace.

What I will say: the pattern is the first day. Every time the early church gathered on it, they were saying the same thing we say Sunday morning — He is risen. The work is finished. We don't have to earn anything today.

I can't preach law where God has preached grace. But I can point you to a pattern — gather, rest, remember, repeat.

Three Practices:

  1. Prioritize the Lord's Day for corporate worship — not from law, but from love for Christ and His Church. Hebrews 10:25 “25 Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”
  2. Build rhythms of rest. The creation ordinance of shabbat/nuakh is wise for all people. You are not a machine.
  3. Use the Lord's Day to declare the resurrection. Every Sunday is a small Easter.
sermons.notesText:
Introduction

At Crown College, someone told me it was okay to borrow someone else's conviction until you had your own.

I had borrowed mine. From my mom. Single mom. She worked hard and carried a lot. But Sunday was different. Sunday was set apart. There was a gravitational pull around that day I could not shake. Not messing with Sunday was somehow foundational to who I was. I didn't have the theology. I just had her.

A borrowed conviction will hold you for a while. Eventually life gets hard enough that you need something you actually own.

Today I'm not asking you to adopt my view of Sunday. I'm asking you to walk through the whole Bible on this question and come out the other side with something that belongs to you.

The Framework 

The Passover was fulfilled for us — in Christ 

The Law was fulfilled for us — in Christ 

The Sabbath was fulfilled for us — in Christ

Two Extremes Nobody Here Actually Lives:

Extreme 1 — Legalistic Sabbatarianism: Saturday kept under full Mosaic and rabbinic regulation.
Five examples still practiced: no light switches, no carrying outside an eruv, no tearing paper, no cooking, no driving or machinery.

Extreme 2 — Rest doesn't matter: Seven-day work weeks, no Lord's Day priority, no rhythm of rest.
Physically: fatigue, burnout, breakdown.
Spiritually: no time for God or family — leads to drift.

Most of us live between these. Not legalists. Not dismissers. Just people who inherited a Sunday habit and never examined it.

The Sabbath Was Always About More Than a Day

Two Hebrew Words:

SHABBAT — To stop working. Like clocking out at the end of a shift. NUAKH — To dwell. To settle. Like arriving at your grandmother's house for the holidays, putting your bag down, and exhaling. Rest as presence, not just cessation.

God didn't just stop working on Day Seven. He moved in with His people. The garden was the first dwelling place — rest as relationship.

Genesis 2:2–3 “2 And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. 3 And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.” 

Two things to observe:

Completion, not exhaustion — satisfaction in finished work 

Pre-Mosaic — before any law was given, before Moses, Israel, or Sinai Pattern, not command — a rhythm wired into creation itself

The Sabbath was never really about a day. It was always about a relationship.

Israel Got the Picture, But Missed the Point

The Manna Test — First Commanded Sabbath, Before Sinai:

Exodus 16:28–29 “28 And the LORD said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? 29 See, for that the LORD hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.” 

A covenant test for Israel specifically — not a universal creation command applied to all peoples.

Codified at Sinai:

Exodus 20:8–10 “8 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. 9 Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: 10 But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:” 

Exodus 31:16–17 “16 Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. 17 It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.” 

Key observations:

Specific audience: Israel. Not the nations. Not the Church.

Covenant sign — marking a specific people in a specific covenant

Death penalty for violation — Exodus 31:14; Numbers 15:32-36 — civil/national law for a theocracy

The Second Grounding:

Deuteronomy 5:15 “15 And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.” 

Exodus 20 grounds the Sabbath in creation. 

Deuteronomy 5 grounds it in the Exodus from Egypt. That national/redemptive grounding makes no sense applied to Gentile believers.

Sabbath Year and Jubilee:

Leviticus 25:1–4 “1 And the LORD spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying, 2 Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the LORD. 3 Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; 4 But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.” 

Every seventh year: the land rested.

Every 50th year (Jubilee): debts cancelled, property restored, slaves freed.

Civil/theocratic law for a land-owning nation under direct divine governance. Not transferable to the Church.

The Problem — The Picture Became the Prison:

By the time Jesus arrives, the Pharisees had buried the Sabbath under 613 regulations. The rest God intended had become an exhausting legal performance.

Matthew 11:28-29

Matthew places this BEFORE the Sabbath controversies in chapter 12. Jesus is not rescheduling the Sabbath — He is announcing He has become what it always pointed to.

Israel had the picture for 1,500 years. Then the reality showed up and said "Come to me."

Historical Books: The Ignored Sabbath

Nehemiah 13:18 “18 Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.” 

Notice what Sabbath-breaking looked like:

Working in the fields  

Hauling goods  

Operating businesses  

Buying and selling  

Conducting normal commerce

Nehemiah's concern is not that they failed to attend worship services. His concern is that they ignored the covenant sign God had given Israel and treated the Sabbath like any other day.

Prophets: The Kingdom Sabbath

In the prophets we see it was ignored and also we see propphecy of it continuing during the millennial reign. 

The Sabbath is not abolished in Colossians 2. It is fulfilled for this age. The prophets tell us it will be restored in the Kingdom under Christ's direct reign.

Isaiah 66:23 “23 And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD.” 

Ezekiel 46:1 “1 Thus saith the Lord GOD; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened.” 

The Church doesn't observe the Mosaic Sabbath because we are in a different period of God's redemptive plan — not because God forgot it. He never drops this thread.

The Sabbath Across Scripture — Five Periods:

CREATION: Pattern established. Six and one. Work and rest.

MOSAIC / ISRAEL: Formalised as covenant sign. Shadow pointing forward. 

CHURCH AGE — NOW: Fulfilled in Christ. Lord's Day. Liberty, not law. 

MILLENNIUM — FUTURE: Renewed under Christ's direct reign. All nations worship. 

NEW CREATION: Eternal Sabbath. God dwelling with His people. Revelation 21:3 “3 And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” 

The Sabbath runs from Genesis 2 all the way to the New Creation. God never drops this thread.

What Jesus Did to the Sabbath

1. Jesus Is Lord of the Sabbath:

Mark 2:27–28 “27 And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: 28 Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.” 

Not correcting a technicality. 

Asserting ownership over the whole institution. 

If He is Lord over the Sabbath, He determines its meaning and its fulfillment.

Matthew 12:6 “6 But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.” 

Greater than the temple = greater than everything the temple and its calendar pointed to.

2. The Finished Work:

Hebrews 10:1, Hebrews 10:9–10 “9 Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. 10 By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.” 

Hebrews 4:9–10 “9 There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. 10 For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” 

The word in Hebrews 4:9 is sabbatismos — the only NT occurrence. 

Sabbath-rest. Not a day on a calendar. A person. Entering His rest means ceasing from self-justification, striving, earning what Christ freely gives.

Which Day? 

Sabbatarian Case — held by sincere Christians:

Fourth Commandment is in the Decalogue — moral law does not pass away Sabbath predates Sinai (Genesis 2) — not merely national/civil law 

Matthew 5:17 — "I came not to destroy, but to fulfil" — they read this as uphold, not complete No explicit NT command changing the day from Saturday to Sunday

This view has been held by sincere, faithful Christians. We engage it respectfully.

Lord's Day Case — Three Anchor Texts:

1. Replace the shadow with the Person

Colossians 2:16–17 “16 Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: 17 Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” 

Paul calls the Sabbath days themselves a shadow — not the way you keep them. The substance is Christ. When you have the reality, the picture no longer binds.

2. Day-observance matter of liberty

Romans 14:5 “5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” 

Day-observance placed in the category of conscience and liberty. You cannot do that with "do not murder." That single placement is decisive.

3. Non binding law

Galatians 4:9–10 “9 But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? 10 Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years.” 

Paul's alarm is stunning. It only makes sense if the Mosaic calendar has passed as binding law for the Church.

The Resurrection Sunday

John 20:19 “19 Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.” 

Think about John 20:19. The disciples are behind locked doors. Terrified. 

The Sabbath has come and gone. Saturday ended with a sealed tomb and a scattered church. 

Then — on the first day of the week — Jesus walks through the wall.

He chose that moment. He chose that day. The first Christian Sunday gathering was not planned by the apostles. It was called by the risen Christ Himself. John 20:26 “26 And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.” 

He did it again the following Sunday with Thomas present.

The Sabbath rest was finished at the cross. The celebration of that rest began on Easter Sunday morning — and it has not stopped since.

The SDA Position — A Different Category:

A Christian who worships on Saturday out of personal conviction is your brother or sister. Romans 14 covers that. We differ, but the gospel we share is not undone by that difference.

The SDA system is a different matter — it has made Sabbath-keeping salvation-relevant:

Saturday Sabbath is a test of end-times loyalty — linked to the "mark of the beast" Investigative Judgment (1844) reviews believers' lives for worthiness — undermining the finished work of Christ Ellen White's writings carry quasi-authoritative status alongside Scripture

When the Sabbath is tied to salvation, it is no longer a liberty issue. It has become a gospel issue.

A believer with a Sabbatarian conviction is a brother. A system that makes Sabbath-keeping a test of salvation is a doctrinal error touching the gospel.

We didn't abolish the Sabbath. We fulfilled it — in Christ. And Christ is better than the shadow.

Therefore: Why We Gather on Sunday

The New Testament Pattern:

Acts 20:7 “7 And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.” 

1 Corinthians 16:2 “2 Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.” 

Revelation 1:10 “10 I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,” 

What we lose is the legal obligation to observe Saturday with Mosaic regulations. What we gain is freedom to gather on the Lord's Day in resurrection joy — not from compulsion, but from love.

Early Church Confirmation:

Justin Martyr (c. AD 155): Christians gathered on Sunday because it is the day Jesus Christ rose from the dead.

Ignatius of Antioch (c. AD 110): Christians "no longer observe the Sabbath, but live according to the Lord's Day, on which our life has sprung up through Him."

Within one generation of the apostles. Apostolic pattern from the beginning — not a medieval Catholic invention.

A Pastoral Word:

I want to be honest about something I wrestle with as your pastor.

I want you to hold the Lord's Day in high esteem. I want Sunday to mean something to your family — a genuine weekly declaration that you belong to a risen Saviour.

But here is my tension: I can't bind your conscience where the New Testament gives you liberty. Romans 14 says the strong believer does not despise the one who esteems every day alike. I can't preach law where God has preached grace.

What I will say: the pattern is the first day. Every time the early church gathered on it, they were saying the same thing we say Sunday morning — He is risen. The work is finished. We don't have to earn anything today.

I can't preach law where God has preached grace. But I can point you to a pattern — gather, rest, remember, repeat.

Three Practices:

Prioritize the Lord's Day for corporate worship — not from law, but from love for Christ and His Church. Hebrews 10:25 “25 Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.”  

Build rhythms of rest. The creation ordinance of shabbat/nuakh is wise for all people. You are not a machine. 

Use the Lord's Day to declare the resurrection. Every Sunday is a small Easter.

sermons.title: What Is the Gospel?
sermons.speaker: Trent Cornwell
sermons.notesHtml:
Text: 1 Corinthians 15:1–4

Big Idea: God’s announcement about Christ demands everything.

INTRODUCTION

A. The Question

1. Took Nate Wilkerson to the airport.

2. Someone had put a question to Carsen.

3. Where would you start in telling someone the gospel?

B. The Observation

1. You could start anywhere — God, sin, the cross, resurrection, creation, the law.

2. No matter where you start, you end up in the same place.

3. The story always arrives at the cross.

4. It always demands a response.

5. It always divides eternity.

C. Ten Questions

1. What exactly is the gospel?

2. What gets mistaken for it?

3. Is it really good news or just religious information?

4. Why does anyone even need it?

5. What actually happened at the cross — and how did it work?

6. What does God do to those who receive it?

7. What happens to those who reject it — and why is that just?

8. What about people who never heard?

9. What does a gospel-changed life look like?

10. What are we supposed to do with it?

1 Corinthians 15:1–4 Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you... how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.

D. The Stakes

Accepting the gospel as true determines your eternity. Understanding the implications of the gospel determines your life.

Q1 What Is the Gospel?

  • Gospel Definitions “The gospel is the royal announcement that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, lived a perfect life in our place, died a substitutionary death on the cross for our sins, rose triumphantly from the grave to launch God’s new creation, and is now exalted as King of the world.”

A. The Gospel Is an Announcement

1. Gospel means good news — not general good news.

2. A specific announcement about a specific person and what he accomplished.

3. Not advice about what you should do. An announcement about what has already been done.

4. Mark opens his entire account with the word ‘gospel.’ Jesus’ life, death, and resurrection isn’t just in the gospel — it is the gospel.

  • Mark 1:1 The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

5. This was not improvised. It was promised. It arrived on schedule.

  • Romans 1:1–2 Separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures.)

B. The Four Non-Negotiable Facts

1. Christ died for our sins. Not as a martyr. As a substitute.

2. He was buried. The death was real, not symbolic.

3. He rose again. The death was defeated, not just endured.

4. He is now exalted as King. Every knee will bow.

  • 1 Corinthians 15:3–4 How that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures. Philippians 2:9–11 Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

5. Paul gives us four facts as the irreducible minimum. Nothing added. Nothing removed.

C. The Problem of Sin

1. Every person is made for God and restless without him.

  • Augustine — Confessions, Book 1 “Thou hast made us for thyself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it finds its rest in thee.”

2. There is none righteous. Not one.

  • Romans 3:10–12 As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.

3. All have sinned and come short of the glory of God.

  • Romans 3:23 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.

4. Sin is not bad behavior. It is rebellion against the Creator.

5. Sin doesn’t just make you guilty. It separates you from God.

  • Isaiah 59:2 But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.

D. The Justice of God

1. God is merciful. God is also just. Exodus 34 holds both in the same breath.

  • Exodus 34:6–7 The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty.

2. A judge who dismisses charges because he loves the defendant is not a good judge. He is a corrupt one.

3. The wages are fixed.

  • Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

E. The Gospel and Gospel Implications

1. The Gospel — the narrow. What a person must believe to be saved.

2. Gospel Implications — the broad. Every promise God secured through Christ.

3. The Gospel is the door to everything in Gospel Implications.

  • Gospel Definitions “The gospel story is the Scriptural narrative that takes us from creation to new creation, climaxing with the death and resurrection of Jesus at the center.”

4. You cannot reach Gospel Implications without first going through The Gospel.

  • Acts 10:43 To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.

5. The cross is not one part of the good news. It is the door through which all of it is entered.

→ The gospel is the announcement that Christ died, was buried, and rose — the only door to everything God has promised.

Now that we know what the gospel is — we need to know what it isn’t.

Q2 What Gets Mistaken as the Gospel?

1. Three things get mistaken for the gospel consistently.

2. None of them are the gospel.

3. Knowing the difference is not academic — it is eternal.

A. Moralism

1. Moralism says do better and God will accept you.

2. Oldest religion in the world. Most natural one.

3. Puts the work back on you that only Christ could accomplish.

4. Two outcomes. Proud people who think they are succeeding. Broken people who know they are not.

5. It never produces free people.

6. Three men who tried it harder than you ever will.

  • Luther — On his years as a monk “I was a good monk, and I kept the rule of my order so strictly that I may say that if ever a monk got to heaven by his monkery it was I. All my brothers in the monastery who knew me will bear me out. If I had kept on any longer, I should have killed myself with vigils, prayers, reading, and other work.” John Wesley — Journal, returning from Georgia “I went to America to convert the Indians; but, oh, who shall convert me?” John Bunyan — Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners “My neighbours did take me to be a very godly man... and indeed, so it was, though yet I knew not Christ, nor grace, nor faith, nor hope; and truly, as I have well seen since, had I then died, my state had been most fearful.”

7. Luther tried religion. Wesley tried ministry. Bunyan tried morality.

8. Every road that bypasses the cross ends in the same place.

When you sin — what is your first instinct?

9. Minimize. It wasn’t that bad. God knows my heart.

10. Compensate. I’ll pray more. Do better. Make it up.

11. Both responses are Luther before the tower. Managing your account with God by your own activity.

12. No flesh. Not the sincere ones. Not the ones really trying. No flesh.

  • Galatians 2:16 Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
  • Galatians 1:8 But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.

B. The Prosperity Gospel

1. Trades the cross for comfort.

2. Promises Jesus came to make you healthy, wealthy, successful.

3. Jesus promised tribulation. Paul promised persecution.

4. A gospel measured by circumstances has no category for Calvary.

5. The man who invented the gospel died on a cross.

  • John 16:33 In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
  • 2 Timothy 3:12 Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.

C. Social Reform

1. Announces the kingdom without telling anyone how to enter it.

2. Not incomplete gospel. Bad news dressed as good news.

3. You are announcing a future the person has no way of reaching.

4. You cannot fix the sin in hearts by fixing the systems those hearts corrupt.

5. The power is in the announcement, not the movement.

  • Bunyan — Pilgrim’s Progress “Mr. Formalist and Mr. Hypocrisy are on the road — right direction, right path, right appearance — but they climbed the wall instead of going through the Wicket Gate. You can follow Jesus’ example, do works of mercy, live kingdom values, and never have come to Christ. The gate is the cross. There is no other entry.”

6. The power is in the announcement.

  • Romans 1:16 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.
  • Any gospel that does not deal with sin and the cross is not good news. It is no news at all.

→ Anything that bypasses the cross is not the gospel.

So what did it actually take for the gospel to be true? What made it work?

Q3 What Are the Implications? — 12 min

■ What Did Christ Do?

A. Substitution

1. He died instead of us. Not alongside us. Instead of us.

2. He took what was ours. He gave what was his.

3. The exchange is total and runs entirely in one direction.

4. He who had no sin became sin so we who had no righteousness could receive his.

  • 2 Corinthians 5:21 For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.

5. The just for the unjust.

  • 1 Peter 3:18 For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit.

6. His wounds, our healing.

  • Isaiah 53:5 But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.

B. Satisfaction

1. God’s wrath against sin was fully absorbed. Not postponed. Not reduced. Fully absorbed.

2. The debt was not negotiated down. It was paid in full.

3. The standard was not lowered. The payment met it completely.

  • Romans 5:8 But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
  • Hebrews 2:17 Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

C. Vindication

1. The resurrection is the Father’s public declaration that the payment was accepted.

2. Without it you have no proof the transaction was complete.

3. The empty tomb is the receipt.

  • 1 Corinthians 15:17 And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.
  • Jesus did not just show love at the cross. He secured salvation at the cross.

What Does God Give?

D. What God Does to Those Who Receive It

1. Three things happen when a person repents and believes. All permanent. All God’s work.

2. Justification — God declares you righteous in Christ. Not a feeling. A legal verdict that cannot be undone.

  • Romans 5:1 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

3. Reconciliation — The relationship is not improved. It is created where there was none. You were an enemy.

  • Romans 5:10 For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

4. Adoption — Not a servant. Not a tolerated guest. A child.

  • Romans 8:15 For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

E. Heaven — For Those Who Receive

1. Heaven is not a reward for good people.

2. It is the inheritance of those who are in Christ.

3. God does not weigh your record. He sees the righteousness of his Son.

4. That standing cannot be undone.

  • Romans 8:1 There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
  • John 14:2–3 In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also. 1 John 5:11–12 And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

F. Hell — For Those Who Reject

1. Hell is not an overreaction. It is the just consequence.

2. Every person carries a debt they cannot pay. God provided the payment.

3. To reject Christ is to refuse the payment and stand before a holy God in your own record.

4. Condemned already.

  • John 3:18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
  • 2 Thessalonians 1:8–9 In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power. Revelation 20:15 And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

G. What About Those Who Never Heard?

1. The assumption: condemned for missing the gospel.

2. The truth: condemned for sinning against the God they already knew.

3. Creation leaves every person without excuse.

  • Romans 1:18–20 For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them... For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen... so that they are without excuse.

4. God’s moral law is written on every conscience.

  • Romans 2:14–15 For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness.

5. The question is not: did they hear about Jesus? The question is: did they live up to the light they already had?

7. No one has.

8. One name. No other road.

  • Acts 4:12 Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
  • John 14:6 Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

→ The gospel justifies, reconciles, adopts — and determines your eternity.

If these are the implications — what does a life shaped by the gospel actually look like?

Q4 What Behavior Does It Create? — 6 min

1. Grace produces what law could only demand.

2. The behavior is always fruit. Never root.

A. Holiness

1. The gospel does not demand holiness to earn acceptance.

2. It announces acceptance — and that produces the desire to be holy.

3. Grace teaches what fear never could.

  • John Wesley — after Aldersgate “The same man who returned from Georgia unable to convert himself went on to preach over 40,000 sermons and see revival sweep England. The gospel produced in forty years what moralism could not produce in forty days.”

1. You did not earn this. You received it.

2. Everything you have in Christ is a gift.

3. That kills pride at the root.

4. Nothing to boast in but Christ.

  • Ephesians 2:8–9 For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.

1. The standard for how you treat others is now what Christ did for you.

2. You forgive because you have been forgiven.

3. You serve because you have been served.

4. The gospel does not just instruct love. It generates it.

The king is furious — not because the forgiveness was conditional, but because it clearly never reached the servant. He received it as information. He never inhabited it.”

1. You do not graduate from the gospel.

2. You go deeper into it.

3. The Christian life is not a movement away from the gospel toward maturity.

4. It is a movement into greater understanding of what the gospel already secured.

5. The believer who drifts from it does not become more spiritual. He becomes more religious.

Text: 1 Corinthians 15:1–4 

Big Idea: God’s announcement about Christ demands everything.

INTRODUCTION 

A. The Question

1. Took Nate Wilkerson to the airport.

2. Someone had put a question to Carsen.

3. Where would you start in telling someone the gospel?

B. The Observation

1. You could start anywhere — God, sin, the cross, resurrection, creation, the law.

2. No matter where you start, you end up in the same place.

3. The story always arrives at the cross.

4. It always demands a response.

5. It always divides eternity.

C. Ten Questions

1. What exactly is the gospel?

2. What gets mistaken for it?

3. Is it really good news or just religious information?

4. Why does anyone even need it?

5. What actually happened at the cross — and how did it work?

6. What does God do to those who receive it?

7. What happens to those who reject it — and why is that just?

8. What about people who never heard?

9. What does a gospel-changed life look like?

10. What are we supposed to do with it?

1 Corinthians 15:1–4 Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you... how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.


D. The Stakes

Accepting the gospel as true determines your eternity. Understanding the implications of the gospel determines your life.


Q1 What Is the Gospel? 

Gospel Definitions “The gospel is the royal announcement that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, lived a perfect life in our place, died a substitutionary death on the cross for our sins, rose triumphantly from the grave to launch God’s new creation, and is now exalted as King of the world.”


A. The Gospel Is an Announcement

1. Gospel means good news — not general good news.

2. A specific announcement about a specific person and what he accomplished.

3. Not advice about what you should do. An announcement about what has already been done.

4. Mark opens his entire account with the word ‘gospel.’ Jesus’ life, death, and resurrection isn’t just in the gospel — it is the gospel.

Mark 1:1 The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

5. This was not improvised. It was promised. It arrived on schedule.

Romans 1:1–2 Separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures.)


B. The Four Non-Negotiable Facts

1. Christ died for our sins. Not as a martyr. As a substitute.

2. He was buried. The death was real, not symbolic.

3. He rose again. The death was defeated, not just endured.

4. He is now exalted as King. Every knee will bow.

Philippians 2:9–11 Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.


5. Paul gives us four facts as the irreducible minimum. Nothing added. Nothing removed.

C. The Problem of Sin

1. Every person is made for God and restless without him.

Augustine — Confessions, Book 1 “Thou hast made us for thyself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it finds its rest in thee.”


2. There is none righteous. Not one.

Romans 3:10–12 As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.


3. All have sinned and come short of the glory of God.

4. Sin is not bad behavior. It is rebellion against the Creator.

5. Sin doesn’t just make you guilty. It separates you from God.

Isaiah 59:2 But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.


D. The Justice of God

1. God is merciful. God is also just. Exodus 34 holds both in the same breath.

Exodus 34:6–7 The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty.


2. A judge who dismisses charges because he loves the defendant is not a good judge. He is a corrupt one.

3. The wages are fixed.

E. The Gospel and Gospel Implications

1. The Gospel — the narrow. What a person must believe to be saved.

2. Gospel Implications — the broad. Every promise God secured through Christ.

3. The Gospel is the door to everything in Gospel Implications.

Gospel Definitions “The gospel story is the Scriptural narrative that takes us from creation to new creation, climaxing with the death and resurrection of Jesus at the center.”


4. You cannot reach Gospel Implications without first going through The Gospel.

1. Moralism says do better and God will accept you.

2. Oldest religion in the world. Most natural one.

3. Puts the work back on you that only Christ could accomplish.

4. Two outcomes. Proud people who think they are succeeding. Broken people who know they are not.

Luther — On his years as a monk “I was a good monk, and I kept the rule of my order so strictly that I may say that if ever a monk got to heaven by his monkery it was I. All my brothers in the monastery who knew me will bear me out. If I had kept on any longer, I should have killed myself with vigils, prayers, reading, and other work.”

sermons.title: What the Bible Says About Eternity
sermons.speaker: Trent Cornwell
sermons.notesHtml:
Introduction

Before we open the Bible, we need to clear away something that over a billion people believe about eternity — and that most Protestants cannot explain. It is called purgatory. And it did not come from Scripture.

A. 1517 — The Year Everything Broke Open

• October 31, 1517 — Martin Luther nails 95 theses to the Castle Church in Wittenberg

• His target: indulgences — certificates sold granting release from time in purgatory

“As soon as the coin in the coffer rings, the soul from purgatory springs.” — Johann Tetzel, c. 1517

• The Protestant Reformation was, in large part, a war over purgatory

B. What the Catholic Church Teaches

Definition: A state of purification for those dying in God’s grace but not yet fully purified — not eternal, everyone there is going to heaven

• The living can shorten a soul’s time there through prayer, masses, and indulgences

• It took 1,200 years and multiple councils to build this doctrine

Council of Florence, 1439: First full official definition. Required belief in purgatory.

Council of Trent, 1563: Defined as binding doctrine in response to the Reformation. Denial = anathema.

No doctrine requiring 1,200 years of debate to establish was in the original text.

C. The Texts Catholics Use — and Why They Don’t Hold

2 Maccabees 12:44 “44 For if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead.”

44 For if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead.

  1. The primary Catholic proof text.
  2. The problem:
  3. 2 Maccabees is not in the Bible.
  4. Jesus never quoted it.
  5. The NT never quotes it.
  6. A doctrine cannot stand on a book the original readers did not accept as Scripture.

Matthew 12:32 “32 And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.”

32 And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

  1. Catholics argue this hints at forgiveness after death.
  2. But here Jesus is closing a door, not opening one.
  3. He is contrasting this present age with the coming kingdom — not this life with purgatory.

1 Corinthians 3:13–15 “13 Every man’s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is. 14 If any man’s work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. 15 If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.”

13 Every man’s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is. 14 If any man’s work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. 15 If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

  1. Catholics read this as purifying fire after death.
  2. Paul is describing the Judgment Seat of Christ — where a believer’s works are tested, not the person.
  3. The person is already saved before the fire arrives.

D. Why Scripture Rejects Purgatory

Hebrews 9:27 “27 And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:”

27 And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:

  1. Two steps only: death, then judgment.

  4. Lake of Fire: The final, eternal hell. The second death. Still future — Revelation 20.
